# 2 Baruch Chapter 32 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Second Fast and Dialogue

---

**32:1** For whatever is now is nothing; but whatever is coming will be great. For all that is corruptible will pass away, and everything that dies will depart, and the present time will be forgotten, and there will be no remembrance of this age, because that which comes is coming quickly.

**32:2** For the souls of the righteous who are now in distress know what has been prepared for them, and on account of this they will not be distressed.

**32:3** But as for us — if we did not know that we are in distress, we would understand nothing; for we know that the distress of this world will not last.

**32:4** And I said to them further: Will not all these distresses pass away from us? And will there not come a time of rest for us? Behold — Zion will be built up again, and the offerings will be restored, and the priests will return to their place, and the peoples will return to the land.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering. Key decisions: "corruptible" (v.1) preferred over PNEUMA's "perishable" — "corruptible" is the standard 2 Baruch anthropological category; "the distress of this world will not last" (v.3) supplied as an implied complement following LOGOS; "offerings" (v.4) preferred over PNEUMA's "sacrifices" as slightly more formal.*
